As, I imagine, a lot of users here who participate in online discussions, I have a fair amount of bookmarks consisting of articles and news stories for future reference. Today I referenced a certain page in a discussion and an user pointed out that it was offline. The other day I wanted to copy a quote from a text I read a few years ago and the site was no longer. So I was wondering if there is an extension, a script, or an application that would save all my bookmarks to .html files to read offline. Archiving to archive.is would be acceptable, though saving to file would be better. If this post gets enough attention but no solution, I'm willing to make such a script (for Firefox).
Is there a way to backup all your bookmarks (the content of the websites, not just the bookmarks themselves)?

There's also httrack. Its man page is tortuous and the explanations often unclear but I think this might store one page properly:

httrack url -n -r1 -s0

Explanation:

-n: "get non-html files near an html file" (it should download externally linked images as well)

-r1: link depth 1, which means actually scan the url

-s0: don't obey robots.txt

You might need to set -F (the user agent/browser id) as well. This doesn't seem to download a compete frameset if the site is still using frames (!). Finally, it seems to be best to store each link in its own directory, otherwise it seems to overwrite the previous site.
